packet.headline_seed: Australia news live:New Victorian premier Ben Carroll says ‘change starts today’ and pledges construction sector royal commission
packet.description_seed: Follow updates live Jacinta Allan resigns as Victorian premier before leadership challenge by Ben Carroll Who is Ben Carroll? Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast ACTU president says now is the ‘right time’ to leave Michele O’Neil, the president of the Australian Council of Trade Unions, said it’s the “right time” to leave after she announced her departure alongside ACTU secretary Sally McManus . We thought about this and we just think that it’s time for renewal. The union movement is in good shape. We’ve seen changes in workers’ rights that have made a big difference in workers’ lives. We’ve seen the union movement starting to grow for the first time in decades. And next year will be the 100th anniversary of the ACTU. So we think it’s time for a new leadership team to come in. We have a debt heading towards $200bn in this state. We have teachers out striking in the streets because the state government and Ben Carroll can’t secure a pay deal. We have holes in the roads. You need a majority government to fix those problems, and you need someone with a plan. Now he might performatively call a royal commission tokenistically, now that he’s become leader, but that’s not out of sincere concern about corruption. That’s out of sincere concern about the polls and what that means for Victorian Labor. Continue reading...

clean_source_blocks.text: One of the Victorian Labor party’s signature policies has been its focus on infrastructure. During the first term of the Daniel Andrews government, the party promised to remove 50 train level crossings across the state. The government then moved onto bigger and even more ambitious projects. The state’s Big Build project, which involved the construction of major road and rail infrastructure has now become a political problem for the government. Allegations of corruption and the involvement of organised crime have dominated news coverage and the issue has haunted the government. Read more: How the ‘Big Build’ corruption allegations brought down the Victorian premier This has also led to a deepening division between Allan, who resisted calls to establish a royal commission, and others within Labor who were more favourable to such an investigation.

After a tumultuous 24 hours, the Labor Party in Victoria has decided it will have Ben Carroll as its new leader and therefore Premier of Victoria. This is after the state’s attorney-general Sonya Kilkenny, also nominated herself for the leadership following Premier Jacinta Allan stepping down this morning. Kilkenny later pulled her candidacy - had the contest gone ahead, Labor would have been be embroiled in a weeks-long process of selecting their new leader. Avoiding such a drawn-out process was a wise decision for the party, especially as there are just four months before the next election in Victoria. For Carroll, however, winning the top job is just the start of the challenges he confronts as premier. There are several critical areas that need his urgent attention.

Carroll has an opportunity to demonstrate a fresh approach. Calling a royal commission into this matter can serve as an important signal that Labor is under new management. This is a bread-and-butter issue for state governments. In Victoria, crime has become a prominent political issue. While there is a sense crime levels may be on the decline, the state’s police minister described it as “unacceptably high” just weeks ago. The government had implemented new laws to curb youth crime, dubbed “adult time for violent crime”. But some within Labor wanted further action. In recent months, Carroll appeared to be agitating for tougher laws. He had previously indicated his support for adopting a “zero tolerance” approach to crime in the state.
